subject: Upfront commit & ramped credits — proposal and ask
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@rapidlytics.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring an upfront commit (12–18 mo)

Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency and the observability surface. We're evaluating an upfront commit (12–18 months) to get better unit economics but would like a ramped minimum and some near-term credits to help bootstrap usage while we integrate. High-level asks:  
- 12–18 month term (flexible on exact months)
- Credits to cover months 1–3 (to hit product/eng milestones)
- Ramped minimums: lower floors early, step up over quarter 1–2
- Clear overage pricing after the commitment

Can you send a proposal that shows a couple of pricing options (12m vs 18m), what discounts or credits you can do, and an example ramp schedule? We need something we can show finance next week.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
CTO, RapidLytics
oliver@rapidlytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@rapidlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring an upfront commit (12–18 mo)

Oliver — really appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a short proposal (Redwood-Proposal-RapidLytics-v2.pdf) plus a spreadsheet with a few ramp scenarios (Ramp-Schedule-v3.csv). TL;DR options we can move quickly on:  

Option A — 12 months, upfront: 25% term discount + $60k one-time integration credit (applies to first 3 months). Minimum ramp: 40% of forecasted committed tokens M1, 65% by M4.
Option B — 24 months, staged commit (we can present as 18 months too): 18% term discount, larger credits $90k, with a 3-step ramp (30% → 60% → 85%).

Key notes:  
- Credits are applied as dollar credits against invoice; can be used for overages in months 1–3.
- We’re willing to include a limited SLA credit (10% invoice credit) if latency SLOs missed in first 6 months; tighter SLA terms require legal signoff.
- We can put an automatic fallback to hosted smaller model if committed capacity is exceeded (to avoid catastrophic failures).

Next steps I propose: 1) you pick Option A or B (or we model hybrid), 2) we update the SOW and pricing sheet, 3) DocuSign routing to your procurement. If helpful, we can also do a short MAU (mutual action plan) to track milestones.

Attaching: Redwood-Proposal-RapidLytics-v2.pdf; Ramp-Schedule-v3.csv; SOW_RapidLytics.xlsx

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0221
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@rapidlytics.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring an upfront commit (12–18 mo)

Oliver — quick follow on from Rafael's options: if you want faster relief on spend during the integration phase, we can front-load more of the credits into months 1–2 and tighten the ramp requirement in months 1–3 (e.g., 25% → 50% → 75%) in exchange for a slightly longer commit (18 months). That structure lets you get to feature parity while keeping your initial cash outlay low.

Also looping in Dev for any technical constraints on cold-starts/kv-cache sizing that could affect early month usage.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@rapidlytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Seed Ops Team <procure@rapidlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring an upfront commit (12–18 mo)

Thanks Rafael / Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:  
1) Can you provide an explicit table that shows committed tokens, effective $/1k tokens with discount, and how credits reduce month 1–3 invoices?
2) We need to understand whether credits are refundable or strictly applied to invoices (procurement prefers applied credits, not refunds).
3) Can you confirm whether the SLA credit language (10%) is a hard commitment or placeholder until legal reviews? We need to know if it will be baked into the SOW for initial signature.

If you can get an updated pricing table and an SOW with the credits language and DocuSign link, procurement can route it quickly — target is to have a PO in place by the first week of March.

Oliver
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@rapidlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring an upfront commit (12–18 mo)

Oliver — appreciate the precise asks. Quick summary of updates and mutual action plan so procurement has what it needs:  

1) Attached "Redwood-Proposal-RapidLytics-v2.pdf" now includes a pricing table per your ask (committed tokens, $/1k after discount, credit application example). Credits are non-refundable and apply as dollar credits against invoices (can be used for overages in months 1–3).
2) SLA credit language: we can include the 10% invoice credit in the initial SOW as a performance remedy for missed latency SLOs in the first 6 months (subject to standard exclusions). Legal has approved including this language for signature — we note replacement language may appear if full enterprise SLA is requested later.
3) Ramp: final proposed hybrid structure for an 18-month upfront commit: months 1–3 = 30% floor, months 4–6 = 60% floor, months 7+ = 90% floor. We can tweak values if you need more runway up front.
4) Next steps / timeline:
   - Rafael: update SOW with the credits and SLA language (today) — attached SOW_RapidLytics.xlsx
   - RapidLytics procurement: legal/PO review (target by 2026-03-05)
   - DocuSign route for signature (we'll send link once SOW is accepted)

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/98765 — I'll add the MAU there and set milestones (PO, signature, onboarding kickoff).

If that aligns, I'll prep the DocuSign envelope and route to your procure@ address. Appreciate the speed here — we can provision dedicated capacity as soon as we have the signed SOW.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
